correctness.rationale: For h(x,y)=max(x,y)-x-y+(x^2+y^2)/2, exact expansion gives Delta=d/15-c^2/30-d^2/210 on the two-parameter polynomial density. The parametrization c=14r/(7+r^2), d=rc yields a positive increasing density and exactly zero target for 0<r<1/3; F(x)<x. Direct polynomial Hoeffding-projection integration yields V(r)=(56595+80311r^4-6282r^6)/(7425(7+r^2)^3), with V(0)=1/45 and V strictly decreasing on the declared interval. Standard nondegenerate bounded-kernel U-statistic CLT proves fixed-alternative power below nominal; uniform remainder bounds and a triangular-array Lindeberg theorem prove n^(-1/4) critical detection for linear tilts. The checker performed 18 exact-arithmetic assertions including an independent direct double-integral expectation verification. No finite test is substituted for the CLTs.

originality.rationale: The 2021 arXiv version and 2023 journal article define and calibrate this scalar U-statistic but neither supplies a strictly stochastically ordered smooth zero-signal family, its exact fixed-alternative limiting power, or the quarter-power local detection transition. The earlier beta-characterization paper uses a squared L2 threshold discrepancy, and analogous blind-contrast research records concern different statistics. Generic U-statistic asymptotic theory is acknowledged as a tool, not the new claim.
residual_risks: Earlier specialized work may have independently analyzed the same scalar functional or its smooth zero set; negative semantic search cannot establish absolute priority.
Full scholarly coverage of all historical characterizations and every 2023 journal appendix was not established.
The conclusion is limited to the uncensored scalar statistic; it cannot be transferred to the censored version without new analysis.

value.rationale: An explicit positive, strictly increasing polynomial density with first-order stochastic dominance is completely invisible in population mean to a published uniformity goodness-of-fit statistic. More importantly, a continuum of such alternatives has asymptotic rejection probability below nominal, and the same statistic has a sharp n^(-1/4), rather than n^(-1/2), local detection boundary for the natural first-order tilt. These demonstrate material lack of omnibus power and give precise sensitivity limits for practical calibration; neither is an arbitrary tiny finite numerical improvement.
